Methods

AcquireTransactionLockAsync(string, CancellationToken)

Acquires an exclusive, database-wide lock identified by name, held until the current transaction commits or rolls back. Callers competing for the same name are serialized; different names never block each other.

Task AcquireTransactionLockAsync(string name, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)

Parameters

name string

Lock name. Identifies what is being serialized, e.g. "contract-number:53".

cancellationToken CancellationToken

A cancellation token to observe while waiting for the task to complete.

Returns

Task

A task that completes once the lock is held.

Remarks

Use it to serialize a read-then-write that the schema alone cannot make atomic — allocating the next value of a per-tenant sequence, for instance, where every writer reads the same maximum and collides on a unique index. It is an advisory lock: it guards nothing by itself, only callers that ask for the same name.

A transaction must be active (see BeginTransactionAsync(CancellationToken)). Without one the lock is released as soon as the statement ends and protects nothing, so the call throws instead.

The statement itself lives in the provider package — pg_advisory_xact_lock in NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL, sp_getapplock (LockOwner Transaction) in NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer — behind IDbContextTransactionLock, and is registered by that package's AddDatabase helpers. With no such package in play (an in-memory context built by hand in a test) there is nothing to serialize and the call does nothing.
